title: The residual block
goal:
Implement the two-layer building block of Figure 2. With $\mathcal{F}(x) = W_2\,\sigma(W_1 x)$ and $\sigma$ the ReLU (Section 3.2), the block computes

$$y = \sigma\big(\mathcal{F}(x, \{W_i\}) + x\big)$$

when the shortcut is the identity (Equation 1), and $y = \sigma(\mathcal{F}(x, \{W_i\}) + W_s x)$ when a projection $W_s$ matches the dimensions (Equation 2). The paper omits the biases, and so do you.

Write `residual_block(x, W1, W2, Ws=None)`. The vector `x` is one-dimensional. `Ws=None` means the identity shortcut.
hints: Compute the inner part first: `F = W2 @ relu(W1 @ x)`. There is a ReLU between the two matrices.
The second nonlinearity comes after the addition (Figure 2), so apply `relu` to `F + shortcut`, not to `F` alone.
Pick the shortcut with one line: `x if Ws is None else Ws @ x`.
